frame_ledger.high_reg_save_layout_above_frame: After `add sp,#116` in the epilogue, `pop {r3,r5,r6,r7}` reads sp+116..131 as (r8,r9,r10,r11) in that order -- word0 (sp+116..119) is the lone `push {r7}` (orig r8), words1-3 (sp+120..131) are the `push {r5,r6,r7}` (orig r9,r10,r11) pushed one instruction earlier (i.e. at a LOWER address than the r8 word, since it was pushed first / stack grows down). Then `pop {r5,r6,r7}` reads sp+132..143 (caller r5/r6/r7), then `pop {r0}` reads sp+144 (LR) for the final `bx r0`. Total extra above the 116-byte local frame = 4+12+16 = 32 bytes, matching push{r5,r6,r7,lr}(16)+push{r5,r6,r7}(12)+push{r7}(4).
frame_ledger.correction: An earlier pass in this session mis-read the r6-relative struct (`add r6, sp, #104`) as touching r6+12/r6+16 (sp+116/120), which would have overlapped the r8/r9 save words -- re-reading the .s literally shows r6 is only ever accessed at +0 and +4 (sp+104, sp+108), an 8-byte struct entirely inside the declared 116-byte frame. No overlap; the frame is internally consistent.
